The central subject should dominate the composition. Use strong focal hierarchy: (1) the hero moment, (2) the hobby-defining object or environmental detail, (3) supporting environment or secondary objects, (4) a small delightful detail. Do not give equal visual importance to every object or environmental element in the scene, and do not spread attention evenly across the entire image. Avoid ordinary documentary composition and a cluttered scene with no clear single hero element - instead stage a single emotional or atmospheric peak. Use clean, dynamic linework, polished shading, a bright harmonious palette, subtle rim light, sparkling highlights and small glints where semantically appropriate, stylized steam/wind/dust/paper movement where appropriate, graphic color accents, lively perspective, mild perspective exaggeration, foreground framing elements, and a strong diagonal or circular visual flow when helpful - these effects should create excitement and collectibility, and must NOT turn the scene into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself requires it. Default emotional atmosphere: joyful, engaging, optimistic, energetic, curious, triumphant, exciting, inviting, aspirational; serious subjects may use tension, fascination, determination, revelation, or intellectual excitement, but should not become gloomy, depressing, muted, solemn, or dark prestige-TV realism. Prefer clean, colorful palettes, warm/cool contrast, saturated but controlled hues, a visually memorable palette identity, luminous accents, and attractive color separation between hero and background; avoid beige lifestyle palettes, muddy brown-heavy grading, monochrome editorial restraint, Western cinematic desaturation, and corporate muted color schemes. The artwork must be full-bleed and edge-to-edge. Do NOT draw a card border, white border, rounded frame, decorative frame, printed-paper edge, faux card shell, TCG layout, title bar, stats box, logo badge, corner emblem, rarity symbol, or UI panel - the application adds any card UI later; the generated image itself must be pure artwork. Treat all clothing, footwear, bags, sports and athletic equipment, consumer electronics and devices, tools, instruments, vehicles, and other manufactured products as plain, generic, unbranded designs.
